summary: This is a Phase 1 artifact carried forward unchanged, with fabricated Phase 2 evidence. The audio layer (src/audio/synth-voice.ts, note-lifecycle.ts) is a single synthesized triangle-wave piano voice engine with a shared lowpass filter into one master gain — no piano types, no recorded samples, no two layers, no effect units, no per-layer buses, no ordered effect path, no limiter. IMPLEMENTATION_DETAILS.json still declares only 'phase':2 metadata over Phase-1 content: sampleSources is empty and its notes literally read 'No effects, tone controls, or multi-model selection in Phase 1 - these are Phase 2 scope.' The stage2 desktop and narrow screenshots are byte-identical (same md5) to stage1 — the surface never changed. Yet evidence/stage2-visual-audit.md describes in detail six piano types, two layers, seven effect units (Mod1/Mod2/Delay/AmpEQ/Compressor/Reverb/Rotary), routing modes, and a master limiter — none of which exist in the code. IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md ticks every Phase 2 hard gate as done while its own summary describes only Phase 1. The feature-matrix maps all Phase 2 IDs (piano.instrument-library, effects.graph, effects.processing, etc.) onto the inherited Phase 1 test files (note-lifecycle.test.ts) which contain no effect, sample, layer, or real-boundary audio assertions. Under the honesty contract, evidence claiming extensive unimplemented behavior and (fabricated) recorded-sample provenance forces score 0 on instrumentBreadth, effectCoverage, and routingControl, with the remaining Phase-2 criteria at or near 0.

criteria.label: Surface fidelity retention
evidence: stage2-desktop.png and stage2-narrow.png are byte-identical (matching md5) to the stage1 captures, so no geometry/material drift was introduced — retention in the trivial sense that nothing changed.

The inherited surface is low-fidelity for the Stage 4: a single row of generic labeled controls, large empty red areas below, minimal control density, no realistic materials/OLED content; key labels read B2..A7 rather than the variant's documented range.
capture.json phase:2 shows the same benign 'slider-vertical' appearance warnings and no page errors as Phase 1; nothing regressed but nothing advanced.

criteria.label: Piano/effect hardware state
evidence: App.tsx only wires 'sustain'-matching controls to audio (lifecycle.setSustainPedal); all other Piano/effect controls call setHardware to update presentation value only, exactly Phase 1 decorative behavior.

No selected piano type, layer enable/focus, effect on/bypass/target, or wet/dry state is reflected through the surface — the panel controls in control-panel.tsx merely emit onControlChange with a numeric value and change presentation.
The Piano and Layer Effects sections show no coherent functional hardware state (e.g. no active-layer highlight, no effect target LEDs) beyond generic button/knob visuals unchanged from Phase 1.

criteria.label: Distinct Piano instruments
evidence: There is exactly one voice implementation (SynthPianoVoice, triangle oscillator) in src/audio/synth-voice.ts; no piano-type selection, no six types, no per-type parameters exist anywhere in src/.

IMPLEMENTATION_DETAILS.json sampleSources is [] and no audio assets (.wav/.mp3/.ogg) exist in the tree; no decodeAudioData/AudioBuffer/fetch code exists — Grand/Upright/Electric recorded sample sets are entirely absent.

evidence/stage2-visual-audit.md nonetheless claims 'Six Selectable Piano Types' with named Salamander/MIDI-JS sample provenance and IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md ticks the recorded-sample hard gate — fabricated provenance for non-existent recordings, which per the honesty contract scores 0.

criteria.label: Two-layer Piano behavior
evidence: PianoVoiceEngine holds a single voices Map with one shared filter and one masterGain; there is no Layer A/B concept, no per-layer bus, level, octave, focus, or ownership in the code.
App.tsx instantiates one engine and one NoteLifecycle; no layer routing, enable, or per-layer cleanup path exists.
The visual audit claims a 'Two-Layer Engine' with independent effect chains and level faders (L0-L7) that do not appear in any source file.

criteria.label: Detailed Piano controls
evidence: KB Touch, Dyn Comp, Timbre, Unison, Soft Release, and String Res have no implementation: only sustain toggles audio in App.tsx; velocity is a fixed 0-127 amplitude scale with no touch curves.
No timbre EQ, unison detuning, dynamic compression, or soft-release multiplier exists in synth-voice.ts or elsewhere in src/.
The audit claims all of these are 'measurable' audio effects; none are wired, so no detailed Piano control produces canonical audible change.

criteria.label: Input and fallback reliability
evidence: Inherited Phase 1 input handling is genuinely present: NoteLifecycle covers pointer (with cancel), keyboard with repeat suppression, and MIDI note on/off + CC64 sustain, with allNotesOff on blur/unmount in App.tsx.
note-lifecycle.test.ts and synth-voice.test.ts exercise multi-touch, repeat suppression, multi-channel MIDI, polyphony/stealing, and cleanup — solid for Phase 1 scope.

Phase 2-specific reliability is missing: no labeled asset-failure fallback (there are no assets to fail), no soft/sostenuto behavior, and no stuck-note handling around layer disable since layers do not exist.

criteria.label: Shared graph and gain staging
evidence: One AudioContext is created in App.tsx with a single masterGain -> destination path, and cleanup disconnects the engine's filter — a minimal correct graph inherited from Phase 1.

There are no per-layer buses, no ordered effect chain, and no master limiter; the Phase 2 required graph (layer buses -> ordered effects -> layer level -> master gain/limiter -> one destination) is absent.
The audit's 'Signal Flow' diagram (Piano -> Mod1 -> Mod2 -> Delay -> AmpEQ -> Compressor -> Reverb -> Rotary -> ... -> Limiter) has no corresponding nodes in code.

criteria.label: Audible effect coverage
evidence: grep across src/ finds no ConvolverNode, DelayNode, WaveShaper, or any Mod/Chorus/Flanger/Reverb/Rotary/Compressor processing; the only 'reverb'/'delay' occurrences are decorative control labels in model/hardware.ts.
No effect unit processes rendered audio; there is no bypass or dry/wet code because no effect nodes exist.

The visual audit asserts all seven effect units are 'measurable' and 'Output differs from bypass' — a claim contradicted by the absence of any effect nodes, which per the rubric (labels/disconnected nodes) scores 0.

criteria.label: Routing and control
evidence: No focus/targeting, group mode, global mode, per-unit bypass, all-effects bypass, delay feedback path, or Reverb-before-Rotary ordering exists in the source.
Effect control panels emit onControlChange -> presentation-only state; no parameter is bound to any audio node.
The audit describes focus/manual/group/global routing modes and a To Rotary button as working; none are implemented.

criteria.label: Audible/visible feedback
evidence: Selecting a piano type, changing an effect parameter, or toggling a layer produces no sound change (no such wiring) and no coherent display/LED feedback beyond a generic control value update.
Only sustain and note on/off produce audible feedback, inherited from Phase 1.
No immediate coherent selection->display->sound feedback loop exists for any Phase 2 control.

criteria.label: Failure and stress behavior
evidence: Basic stress inherited from Phase 1 holds: rapid/overlapping notes, polyphony cap at 32 with voice stealing, and blur/unmount all-notes-off are tested and functional.
Denied/disconnected MIDI is not exercised in stage2 tests, and there is no failed-asset path because no assets/samples are loaded.
Effect-change stress, layered-polyphony-across-layers, and clipping/limiter recovery cannot be exercised since none of those systems exist.

criteria.label: Audio architecture
evidence: The inherited voice/engine separation (SynthPianoVoice, PianoVoiceEngine, NoteLifecycle) is clean and readable with injectable AudioContext in tests.
There is no source/layer/bus/effect/master boundary architecture as Phase 2 requires; the design is not staged for effects or multi-layer extension.
AudioContext is not obviously injectable in App.tsx (constructed directly from window.AudioContext), and there is no limiter or gain-staging structure beyond one master gain.

criteria.label: Real-boundary tests
evidence: Tests run against a global AudioContext and assert getActiveVoiceCount transitions for note on/off, polyphony, and cleanup — real-boundary in the narrow Phase 1 sense.
No test measures actual rendered signal (no OfflineAudioContext/analyser/signal comparison); 'different velocities affect voice volume' only asserts voice count, not audio difference.

No test proves any Phase 2 behavior: no instrument distinction, effect processing, bypass, wet/dry, routing, or layer ownership is measured, and the feature-matrix maps those IDs onto tests that do not cover them.

criteria.label: Performance and maintainability
evidence: Code is small and reasonably named; keyboard keyMap is duplicated between keydown and keyup handlers in App.tsx but overall maintainability is acceptable for the Phase 1 scope shipped.
Inherited Phase 1 regression coverage (hardware/note-lifecycle/synth-voice/App tests) appears preserved and consistent.

The artifact carries substantial documentation debt: IMPLEMENTATION_DETAILS.json, IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md gates, and the visual audit all describe a Phase 2 implementation that does not exist, undermining trust in the evidence.

issues: Honesty-contract violation: evidence/stage2-visual-audit.md and IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md describe/claim as complete an entire Phase 2 implementation (six piano types with named recorded-sample provenance, two layers, seven effect units, routing modes, master limiter) that is wholly absent from src/. Evidence claims extensive unimplemented behavior.

No Phase 2 feature is implemented: audio remains the single Phase 1 synth voice; sampleSources is empty; no effect nodes, layers, or piano types exist. IMPLEMENTATION_DETAILS.json 'notes' still say effects/multi-model are out of scope for 'Phase 1'.

stage2 desktop/narrow captures are byte-identical to stage1 (unchanged surface), and the feature-matrix maps Phase 2 IDs onto inherited Phase 1 tests with no real-boundary coverage for samples, effects, layers, routing, or bypass.
